notes:
Top-of-funnel enterprise procurement for Private VPC deployment. Primary concern: encryption posture + KMS integration. Short summary and recent touches below.
- 2026-02-18 discovery call w/ CTO A. Patel + SecOps lead R. Gomez. High level: want strict control over key material; prefer BYOK with HSM. Quote from CTO: "We must never hand keys to a third party; full control is non-negotiable." 
- 2026-02-25 follow-up: sent initial security questionnaire (drive link). They returned with heavy comments on key rotation policy and audit trails.
- 2026-03-02 technical deep-dive (Fireflies ff-20260302-3289). Discussed mTLS design, mutually authenticated client certs between customer VPC and Redwood private control plane; they require mTLS + mTLS for internal service-to-service as well.
- 2026-03-05 POC kickoff for Private VPC (staging within customer AWS account). SE Mei Chen leading. POC scope: deploy inference control plane in customer VPC, validate KMS CMEK integration, confirm envelope encryption and audit log forwarding to customer SIEM.
- 2026-03-08 security review call w/ InfoSec + Legal. Major ask: documented key rotation cadence (they want 90-day rotation), proof of HSM key wrapping, and separation of duties for key admin.
- Notes: they run a hybrid cloud model (AWS primary, Azure DR). Need multi-cloud KMS support and cross-region replication rules for audit logs.

Encryption posture details captured from calls:
- In-transit: require mutual TLS (mTLS) for all control-plane and data-plane connections. Client certs issued by their internal CA; Redwood must accept customer CA bundle. TLS 1.3 required; perfect forward secrecy (PFS) required. Support for client cert revocation lists (CRL/OCSP) mandatory.
- At-rest: all model weights and token caches encrypted. Expect envelope encryption where customer master key (CMK) in HSM/KMS wraps data keys. Support for AWS KMS CMKs (CMEK), Azure Key Vault HSM-protected keys, and GCP CMEK. Option for HW-backed HSM (AWS CloudHSM or external Thales) for attestation.
- Key rotation: customer requires automated rotation of data keys every 90 days and re-wrap with new CMK; root CMK rotation policy must support staged rollouts to avoid downtime. Redwood to provide key-rotation runbook and proof-of-concept for zero-downtime key rollovers.
- Secrets management: prefer HashiCorp Vault for dynamic secrets, with Redwood integration to read ephemeral credentials via Vault AppRole or IAM auth. Vault audit logs must be accessible to customer. Also accept AWS Secrets Manager for legacy teams.
- Access controls: KMS key policies must include cross-account principals and tight IAM roles. Separation of duties: encryption engineers vs operators. Redwood to offer role-based access and audit traces showing which principal performed unwrap operations.
- Audit logging and retention: require immutable audit logs for all key usage/unwrapping and model inference access events. Retention: 7 years for key-use logs; immediate export to their SIEM (Splunk/QRadar). Support for streaming logs (syslog/HTTPS) or S3 exports with object-lock compliance.
- Attestation and compliance: they want HSM attestation docs, SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence for Redwood components in the private stack, and support for customer-run penetration test windows.

POC success criteria:
- Redwood control plane accepts customer CA certs and mTLS handshake passes with mutual auth.
- Encryption at-rest validated: CMK wraps data keys; customer demonstrates ability to disable/rotate keys and cause predictable access failure to validate key-dependence.
- Secrets rotation via Vault working end-to-end; ephemeral creds issued and revoked.
- Audit logs show key unwrap events with principal and timestamp; logs exported to their SIEM automatically.

Next actions (short):
- SE to deliver KMS integration PRD by 2026-03-14 (Mei)
- Security to deliver formal key rotation runbook + HSM attestation template by 2026-03-18
- Legal to draft BYOK SLA amendment; need draft for customer legal review by 2026-03-22

Blockers and risks:
- Legal pushback on BYOK liabilities (customer wants indemnity for key compromise)
- External HSM procurement timeline may extend POC
- Need clarity on cross-region audit log immutability (e.g., object-lock) — customer's compliance team will require proof

Sales notes: strong fit for Redwood Private. Large ARR potential if BYOK + audit retention support accepted. Procurement timeline aggressive; customer expects decision by 2026-06. Tone: technical-first, conservative on handing over secrets.
